reconciled_candidates.label: Bag of Words (BoW)
reconciled_candidates.description: A text representation that counts word occurrences in a document, ignoring order but preserving multiplicity, often forming a document-term matrix.
coverage_criteria: Create a BoW vector for a given document.
Explain the main limitation of BoW (ignoring word order).
Describe the document-term matrix structure.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Single candidate that clearly defines a specific and well-known feature extraction technique.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The 'Bag of Words:' section explicitly describes the method, provides an example ('Tackling is the best part of football'), and shows a document-term matrix via an image.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Bag of Words is a specific, well-known technique that can be assessed with a few questions about its mechanics and limitations.

reconciled_candidates.label: TF-IDF
reconciled_candidates.description: A weighting scheme that scales term frequency by the inverse of document frequency to highlight words that are important to a specific document within a corpus.
coverage_criteria: Compute the TF-IDF score for a term given term frequency and document frequency.
Explain why TF-IDF improves over simple term frequency.
Identify when to use TF-IDF in text analysis.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Standalone concept that introduces a specific numeric weighting method distinct from raw counts.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The 'TF-IDF:' section explains the limitation of Bag of Words and defines TF-IDF with a worked example through an included image.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: TF-IDF is a standalone concept that can be checked by asking about its formula, purpose, and when it is used.

reconciled_candidates.label: One-hot Encoding
reconciled_candidates.description: A sparse representation where each word is a vector of zeros with a single 1 at the index corresponding to the word in the vocabulary.
coverage_criteria: Produce a one-hot vector for a word from a given vocabulary.
Explain the dimensionality problem with one-hot encoding for large vocabularies.
Compare one-hot encoding to dense embeddings.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Distinct concept covering a basic but limited word representation method.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The 'One-hot Encoding:' section describes it as assigning 1 for the present word and 0 for others, and includes an example with the sentence 'The cat sat on the mat.'
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: One-hot encoding is a simple, fundamental idea that can be assessed by asking students to produce or interpret a one-hot representation.

reconciled_candidates.label: Word Embedding
reconciled_candidates.description: Dense, low-dimensional vector representations of words that capture semantic similarities, enabling analogies through vector arithmetic.
coverage_criteria: Explain how word embeddings capture meaning (e.g., similar words have close vectors).
Give an example of an analogy solvable with embeddings.
Contrast word embeddings with one-hot encoding.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Standalone concept introducing the general idea of distributed word representations, which underlies specific methods like Word2Vec.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The 'Word Embedding:' section introduces the need for dense, fixed-size vectors that show word similarity and analogies, and includes a visualization of 7-dimensional embeddings mapped to 2D.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Word embedding is a core concept in modern NLP; it can be checked by asking about its properties and how it differs from earlier representations.

reconciled_candidates.label: Word2Vec
reconciled_candidates.description: A shallow neural network model that learns word embeddings from large corpora using either the Continuous Bag of Words (CBOW) or skip-gram architecture.
coverage_criteria: Distinguish between CBOW and skip-gram training objectives.
Explain how Word2Vec produces dense vectors for words.
Describe a practical use of pre-trained Word2Vec embeddings.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Specific implementation of word embedding; it stands alone as a teachable model within the feature extraction lesson.

extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Word2Vec is a specific, widely-used technique that can be assessed with questions about its architecture and training approaches.

reconciled_candidates.label: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
reconciled_candidates.description: GloVe is an unsupervised learning algorithm for generating word embeddings by factorizing a word co-occurrence matrix, capturing global statistical information.

reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Standalone concept; represents the GloVe embedding method introduced in the self-study.

extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: GloVe is a distinct embedding method; it can be checked by asking about its reliance on global statistics versus local context.

lesson.title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs
lesson.description: O objetivo deste encontro é comparar os sistemas implementados utilizando modelos com Embedding Words e os modelos baseados em extração de características. Ao término do encontro, espera-se que as pessoas desenvolvedoras possam estar familiarizadas com as características comuns destes sistemas e suas peculiaridades de implementação. Também será realizada uma familiarização com o desenvolvimento de API Python.
